environment: Apple M5 Max, macOS 26.6, Python 3.14.7, build123d 0.11.1; shared developer machine, measured with the one-minute load average below 4; minimum of samples

composite.what: two recognition results and one census over four golden fixtures, rebuilt each iteration
composite.budget_note: Inherited from the previous host, where this two-second arm's minimum-of-five ranged 1.93s to 2.66s over one evening and a ceiling under that spread would have reported the load rather than the code. This box is steadier -- three quiet windows over two hours, on adjacent revisions of this stack, gave 0.863s, 0.866s and 0.898s, a 4.1% spread -- but three windows on a machine other work shares is not enough to tighten a ceiling on, and a check that cries wolf stops being run. The census arm is nineteen times longer and remains the tight one.
composite.baseline_note: 0.972s at a5f1fcc, the branch point, measured on the same box in the adjacent quiet window, against 7918c8a (0.866s) -- the revision of this stack immediately before the one recorded here, and within this arm's own spread of it.

census.what: feature_census over the ten vendored NIST parts and three real gramel parts, imported once
census.baseline_note: 75.032s at a5f1fcc, the branch point, measured on the same box in the adjacent quiet window, against 7918c8a (16.295s) -- the revision of this stack immediately before the one recorded here.

commands: uv run python tools/benchmark_recognition.py --implementation package --workload composite --iterations 5
uv run python tools/benchmark_recognition.py --implementation package --workload census --iterations 3
uv run python tools/benchmark_recognition.py --implementation package --workload census --iterations 3 --check docs/benchmarks/recognition-budget.json
budget_note: The default multiplier, used by any workload that records none of its own. Applied to the census arm, which is long enough to be stable here.
